prompt:
You are an evaluator in a study of visualization tools. The file `screenshot.png` in this folder is a
screenshot (1400 x 900 pixels) of a figure that someone made to answer a question with a public dataset.
Open it with the Read tool and look at it carefully. Do not use any other tool, and do not look for anything
else: score only what you can see in the screenshot.

Question the figure should answer: Overview of several years, detail down to minutes

Score each requirement below with 2 (met), 1 (partial) or 0 (not met), using its rubric. If the figure shows
something that contradicts a ground-truth check, give that requirement at most 1. If there is no figure at
all, every requirement scores 0.

R1. An **overview** shows the whole period 2020–2024 for `tl` at once.
   2 when: all of 2020–2024 visible at once for `tl`
   1 if: part of the range only

R4. Precipitation `rr` is shown in the detail view as its own track or axis, aligned in time with `tl`.
   2 when: `rr` as its own aligned track/axis in the detail
   1 if: not aligned, or missing

R7. Axes are labelled with units (°C, mm per 10 min, UTC). The figure has a title and a one-sentence caption stating the main pattern you see.
   2 when: units (°C, mm/10 min, UTC), title, caption
   1 if: any missing

Ground-truth checks (computed from the data):

- File: 263,088 rows, 2020-01-01T00:00+00:00 to 2024-12-31T23:50+00:00, exactly every 10 minutes,
  no duplicates, **no missing values** (no empty `tl` or `rr`). Columns: `time,station,tl,rr,substation`.
- A deliverable that loads all rows shows 2020 to 2024 without gaps; gaps in the figure mean rows were lost.
- `tl`: maximum **36.7 °C at 2021-07-08T14:00Z**; minimum **−10.1 °C at 2024-01-10T03:40Z**.
  Monthly means from 2.6 °C (Jan) to 22.7 °C (Jul). Days with a maximum ≥ 30 °C: 17 (2020), 19 (2021),
  27 (2022), 30 (2023), 44 (2024).
- `rr`: wettest 10-minute interval **26.7 mm at 2024-08-17T14:40Z** (a summer thunderstorm, a good zoom
  target). Yearly totals: 698.5, 580.1, 463.1, 807.5, 834.8 mm (2020–2024).
- Diurnal cycle in UTC: coolest around 03:00, warmest around 13:00 (mean 9.3 vs 15.7 °C). A figure in
  local time (CET/CEST) shifts this by 1–2 h; R7 asks for UTC.
- Render time in Chromium for the full file: record in `results/scores.csv`, column `render_seconds`.

Answer with ONLY a JSON object, no other text, in this form:
{"R1": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R4": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R7": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}}

answer.result: {"R1": {"score": 2, "reason": "Panel A shows daily mean and min–max of tl for all of 2020–2024 with no visible gaps."}, "R4": {"score": 2, "reason": "Panels B and C show rr in its own track, in mm/10 min, on the same UTC time axis as tl."}, "R7": {"score": 2, "reason": "Axes give °C, mm/10 min and Time (UTC); there is a title and a one-sentence caption on the annual cycle and the 14:40 UTC rain burst on 17 Aug 2024."}}
